sources.entry: funasr - Industrial-grade speech recognition toolkit with speaker diarization and emotion detection.

summary.one_liner: FunASR is an open-source speech recognition toolkit from ModelScope offering ASR, VAD, punctuation, speaker diarization, emotion and audio-event models, with offline, streaming, and CPU/edge deployment options.
summary.what_it_does: The toolkit provides a Python AutoModel interface and a funasr CLI for transcribing audio files into text, optionally with timestamps, speaker labels, and SRT/JSON output. Pipelines can combine ASR with FSMN-VAD (or optional Silero VAD), ct-punc punctuation, and CAM++ speaker embeddings. A streaming mode processes audio in chunks with a per-session cache for live transcription. Separate models cover emotion recognition (emotion2vec+large) and audio events (SenseVoiceSmall). The README also documents a FastAPI-based funasr-server with an OpenAI-style transcription endpoint, a Docker streaming runtime, and a llama.cpp/GGUF build that runs as a binary without Python. The README lists several third-party models (MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize, Qwen3-ASR, GLM-ASR-Nano, Whisper) with notes on their separate licenses.
use_cases: Transcribe audio or video recordings to text
Generate SRT subtitles from audio files
Self-host a speech recognition HTTP API
Run offline speech recognition on CPU or edge devices
how_to_run: python -m pip install funasr fastapi uvicorn python-multipart
notable: Model zoo covers ASR (SenseVoiceSmall, Paraformer, Fun-ASR-Nano), VAD, punctuation, speaker embeddings, and emotion models in one toolkit
Native CPU/edge build via llama.cpp with GGUF weights and no Python at runtime, with Vulkan and CUDA packages
Streaming transcription with chunked input and per-session cache
CLI designed for scripting and AI agents, with JSON and SRT output
Optional MCP server and OpenAI-compatible API for agent frameworks
caveats: Model weights carry separate licenses from the MIT-licensed toolkit code; check each model card
Some checkpoints are third-party (e.g., MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize) and support varies by serving backend; the README advises benchmarking on your own audio
The HTTP server is unauthenticated by default and the README says to keep it on loopback unless the security guide is followed
summary.license: MIT License for toolkit source code; pretrained model weights are licensed separately per model card
